> Resolve every protein in the given databases to stable Ensembl gene ids, counted against a caller-supplied, release-pinned gene set, with one outcome per protein and the hash of every input.

Wire verb `genes resolve` · Python `pymzlib.proteins.resolve_genes` (not yet shipped)

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | absent | — | — | One search database (UniProt XML for real answers; a FASTA carries no gene links). Exactly one of path and paths-stdin. |
| `contaminant` | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Load the --path database as contaminants: every protein is contaminant_not_mapped. |
| `paths_stdin` (wire `--paths-stdin`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Databases on stdin, one per line, optionally followed by a tab and 'contaminant' or 'target' (BULK.md §1). |
| `gtf` | `path` | absent | — | — | An Ensembl GTF, plain or .gz; only gene rows are read. Use the primary-assembly GTF (Species.Assembly.Release.gtf.gz) and keep Ensembl's file name, which carries the release. Exactly one of gtf and gene-set; there is no default. |
| `gene_set` (wire `--gene-set`) | `path` | absent | — | — | Instead of gtf: a compact gene table from mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter. It carries the GTF's provenance, so rows are keyed as against the GTF (tested byte-identical). |
| `xref` | `path` | absent | — | — | Optional Ensembl Species.Assembly.Release.uniprot.tsv(.gz): per-row agreement, and a row per gene only Ensembl links (source ensembl_xref). |
| `threads` | `int` | `1` | — | `>= 1, or -1 for every core` | Databases loaded (and hashed) at once. Output identical at any value. |
| `on_error` (wire `--on-error`) | `string` | `fail` | — | `fail \| skip` | As proteins read. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file_count` | `int` | files | never | Databases given. |
| `read_count` | `int` | files | never | Databases read. |
| `failed_count` | `int` | files | never | Databases that failed (on-error skip only). |
| `protein_count` | `int` | proteins | never | Proteins resolved. |
| `record_count` | `int` | rows | never | Rows in columns: at least one per protein; one per gene for multi_gene; plus ensembl_xref rows. |
| `gene_set` | `object` | — | never | {source_file_name, sha256 (of the file's bytes as read: compressed for .gz), release (null: not in the file name), genome_build (null: no #!genome-build header), genebuild_last_updated (null: no header), gene_count}. |
| `xref` | `object` | — | yes: no --xref was given | {source_file_name, sha256, release (nullable), accession_count}. |
| `outcome_counts` | `map<string,int>` | proteins | never | Outcome name -> proteins with it; all six keys always present. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | FASTA proteins (all not_in_source), a GTF with no release or genome build, no xref (agreement unknown, not false). |
| `files` | `object[]` | — | never | As proteins read; search_database_sha256 is set: lower-case hex sha256 of the DECOMPRESSED database, so .xml and .xml.gz agree. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | source_index, source_path, then mzLib's GeneResolutionTsv.Schema headers in its order (a bridge test holds them equal). |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | Column name to per-row values. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_index` | `int` | — | never | Input position. |
| `source_path` | `string` | — | never | Input path. |
| `accession` | `string` | — | never | Verbatim, as the search reported it (a variant suffix kept). |
| `entry_accession` | `string` | — | never | UniProt entry or unversioned RefSeq accession; verbatim when unrecognized. |
| `isoform` | `int` | — | yes: no -N isoform suffix | UniProt isoform number. |
| `namespace` | `string` | — | never | uniprot \| refseq \| unrecognized. |
| `outcome` | `string` | — | never | resolved \| multi_gene \| off_primary_only \| not_in_source \| unrecognized_accession \| contaminant_not_mapped (GeneResolutionTsv.OutcomeName). |
| `n_genes` | `int` | genes | never | Genes the search database links on the gene set's assembly. |
| `gene_id` | `string` | — | yes: the outcome has no gene on the assembly | Stable Ensembl gene id. |
| `versioned_gene_id` | `string` | — | yes: no gene on the row | As the database wrote it (e.g. ENSG00000111640.15); for an ensembl_xref row, built from the GTF's version, or null when the GTF has none. |
| `gene_symbol` | `string` | — | yes: no gene on the row, or the GTF gives it no gene_name | The release's gene_name: a display label, never a key. |
| `gene_biotype` | `string` | — | yes: no gene on the row | The release's gene_biotype ('unknown' when the GTF omits it). |
| `off_primary_genes` | `int` | genes | never | Linked genes outside the gene set (ALT haplotypes, patches, scaffolds): dropped from n_genes, counted here. |
| `uniprot_gene_name` | `string` | — | yes: the entry names no primary gene | The database's primary gene name, as a label. |
| `source` | `string` | — | never | search_database_dbreference, or ensembl_xref for a gene only Ensembl links (it carries the search database's outcome and never changes it). |
| `search_database_sha256` | `string` | — | never | sha256 of the decompressed database. |
| `gene_set_release` | `string` | — | yes: the GTF's file name carries no release | Ensembl release. |
| `gene_set_sha256` | `string` | — | never | sha256 of the GTF as read. |
| `ensembl_xref_agrees` | `bool` | — | yes: no gene on the row, or no --xref: unknown, not false | Whether Ensembl's xref links this accession to this gene. |
| `ensembl_xref_info_type` | `string` | — | yes: Ensembl's xref does not link the pair, or no --xref | Ensembl's strongest evidence: DIRECT, SEQUENCE_MATCH, INFERRED_PAIR. |
| `ensembl_xref_sha256` | `string` | — | yes: no --xref was given | sha256 of the xref file. |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | neither or both of gtf and gene-set; a missing GTF, gene set or xref; any database-selection error proteins read raises |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | a GTF gene row without gene_id (InvalidDataException); an xref whose header is not Ensembl's nine columns; a compact gene table mzLib's reader refuses; a database mzLib cannot parse |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | never raised by this verb |

### Caveats

- The caller supplies and pins the gene set. Use the primary-assembly GTF, not chr_patch_hapl_scaff: counting ALT haplotypes as genes made human release 116 look 6.99% multi-gene when it is 0.36% (mzLib EnsemblGeneSet remarks).
- A FASTA carries no Ensembl links, so every FASTA protein is not_in_source regardless of biology; the result caveats count them.
- Contaminants are never mapped (contaminant_not_mapped), even when they would resolve.
- multi_gene is one row per gene, never a pick.

### Example

```python
genes = pymzlib.proteins.resolve_genes([xml, fasta], contaminants=[bovine], gtf=gtf, xref=xref)
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`genes_resolve_human.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/genes_resolve_human.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.
